name: The Savoy
insider_take: The Savoy isn't just a hotel—it's where Oscar Wilde held court, where Winston Churchill dined nightly, and where the world's first luxury hotel suite was born in 1889.
whats_special: This legendary Art Deco palace is the only hotel in London where you can drive up on the right side of the road (thanks to a special act of Parliament). The American Bar here invented the Hanky Panky cocktail in 1903, and their famous Savoy Grill has been serving prime cuts since 1898. The hotel's Thames-facing suites offer unparalleled views of the London Eye and Parliament.
pro_tip: Book afternoon tea at the Thames Foyer during weekdays—you'll enjoy the same glass cupola and live piano music with fewer crowds and better photo opportunities.
dont_miss: The iconic Savoy Theatre next door (Gilbert and Sullivan's original home), a nightcap at Beaufort Bar with its black-and-gold glamour, and a stroll along the Victoria Embankment—you're just steps from Covent Garden's buzz and the cultural treasures of Somerset House.
pros: Iconic London landmark with legendary Art Deco elegance and historic charm
Prime Covent Garden location with easy access to West End theaters and shopping
World-renowned afternoon tea service and exceptional fine dining restaurants
Impeccable white-glove service and attention to detail befitting royalty
cons: Premium luxury pricing reflecting exclusive heritage status
Historic building layout may have varying room sizes and configurations
